description: Source-alignment record between the Claude skills in this repo and the Codex plugin port in email-love/codex-agents. Its job is to stop a fix from landing in one surface and silently never reaching the other. Update it whenever either surface ships a change that the other should mirror, and stamp lastAlignmentReview when you have checked the two are in sync.

drift.summary: Portsmouth v3 defect fix: semantic-token bind count in Phase 3 step 5 (task #37). New verification line: every non-placeholder solid fill in a module resolves to a variable binding from the audit's Palette, not to a raw hex. Walk every fillable node, list unbound solid fills by node id with the raw hex and the role they should have (brand background, headline text, button background, divider, footer fill). Empty list is the only pass. Placeholder gray fills for editable image regions are the only allowed exception, each named as an intentional placeholder. Portsmouth shipped 43 unbound fills (31 real, 12 placeholder) and every downstream color change had to touch each of the 31 by hand, exactly the state a design system is meant to remove. Bumps converter 1.25.1 to 1.26.0. Closes Codex finding 8.

drift.summary: Portsmouth v3 defect fix: enforcement teeth on Phase 3 step 5 structural rules (task #36). drift.summary: Portsmouth v3 defect fix: send-readiness pass at hand-off (task #35). New '### Send-readiness pass on every campaign' step at the top of Hand-off in the converter. Before the hand-off conversation, walk every mainFrame campaign root and confirm safe to send. Per campaign root: all nine theme keys populated (not empty, since empty is not neutral and the exporter substitutes dark defaults), non-blank emailSubject and emailPreHeader, fallBackFontName is a single family name not a CSS stack, root has a non-generic name (QA roots renamed with 'QA only, do not send' prefix). Per mj-image: href is real URL or explicitly empty for decorative, altText is meaningful copy or empty for decorative. In footer: no placeholder legal, no 'Lorem ipsum', no literal 'Address' string, unsubscribe as merge tag or real URL not '#'. List every violation by node id under 'Send-readiness violations' heading. Empty list is the only pass. Rationale: Portsmouth's Codex review found the delivered file had zero shared hrefs, zero shared altText, blank subject/preheader on all three campaigns, one root with blank lightThemeBackgroundColor, placeholder legal, and literal 'Address' string in footer. Closes Codex findings 3 and 4. Bumps converter 1.24.0 to 1.25.0.

Report Step 7 gets a new required 'Palette' section between Spacing system and Module inventory: source hex, count of fills using it, module list, plus proposed theme colors with every deviation from source hex listed with the delta so a designer approving the theme approves the drift too. Additional source colors not carried into theme roles listed at the bottom. Rationale: Portsmouth's Codex review found four accent primitives lightened from source (Pink #C4014B -> #D03E75, Magenta, Teal, Orange) with no documentation of the drift, and two source colors absent from theme entirely (a decorative green, a bright blue). drift.summary: Portsmouth v2 defect fix (last of queue): inline plugin-data key table + precondition check (task #28). Adds a new '### Precondition check: confirm the references are present' at the top of Phase 2 that reads references/render-spec.md and references/structure.md before starting; on absent files, names what cannot be verified and directs the agent to fetch a fresh bundle or agree a reduced scope with the user (Portsmouth batch hit this four modules in and cost five rounds of design review). Then a new '### The shared plugin data keys the exporter reads (inline, load-bearing)' section carrying the complete `emaillove` shared plugin data key table inline (name, nodeType, nine theme keys on the mainFrame root, optional email meta, fullWidth, stackColumns, reverseStack, href, altText), with what goes where and what it does. Plus a 'Mobile behaviors that are NOT shared plugin data keys' section covering four mobile behaviors Portsmouth spent rounds hunting for that turned out to be Figma-side: full-width mobile button (layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' on mj-button), fluid-on-mobile image (width-relationship to column content width), mobile padding overrides (node properties), mobile column stacking (stackColumns or mj-group). Render spec keeps the prose, worked examples and rationale; the inline table is the irreducible contract that makes the skill functional even when a bundle ships without references. Closes the Portsmouth v2 queue (5 defect fixes shipped, 1 was deprioritized after the packaging bug that caused the original symptom was fixed, this one lands anyway as belt-and-braces). Bumps converter 1.23.0 to 1.24.0.

drift.summary: Portsmouth v2 defect fix: render-once-crop-locally + band-detection measurement techniques + nav bar worked example (task #32). Three additions across both skills. (1) Converter Phase 3 step 1: on an unstructured source, render the whole design at 1:1 once and crop locally per module rather than per-node get_screenshot (which returns loose rectangles without overlapping text, useless on layered z-order files). (2) Audit Step 5 pass 1: same band-detection technique used for finding module boundaries on unstructured pages (rows of pure canvas background between text/imagery are gaps between modules); record y-coordinates on source ref so Phase 3 crops the same pixels. (3) Converter Phase 3 step 5 visual check: on a module that comes out 20-40px too tall (Figma text renders taller than hand-placed boxes report), detect content bands in source PNG and rebuild PNG, diff them, derive exact padding corrections; deterministic two-pass loop instead of eyeballed nudging. (4) Nav bar worked example added to mj-group visual tells: a row of five or more nav links does NOT survive as a group (exporter divides body width by column count, per-link boxes narrower than a single word, breaks words mid-letter); ungrouped columns stack cleanly, one link per row. Portsmouth: band detection got 24 of 28 modules onto source height; nav bar rule saves two attempts. Bumps audit 1.15.0 to 1.16.0 and converter 1.22.0 to 1.23.0.

drift.summary: Portsmouth v2 defect fix: export sniff test added to Phase 3 (task #29). New Phase 3 step 6 'Export sniff test (once per batch)' between per-module verify (step 5) and batch report (now step 7). After individual modules pass step 5, pick one representative module (a multi-column one when possible, since mobile behavior lives in columns), drop a wrapper instance into a temporary email frame on Campaigns, click plugin's Export, read the HTML. Confirm four things: (1) body width matches foundations target email width, (2) `@media only screen and (max-width` block is present, (3) mobile classes exist for anything that should stack or go full-width (`mj-column-per-100`, `mj-b-full`), (4) per-section column widths plus gutters sum to intended content box (a `mj-group` that overflows shows up as a column-sum > body width). Record confirmations in batch report; on a fail, fix the defect Figma-side and re-export, do not open review. Rationale: every check in step 5 is Figma-side, and the plugin's exporter is what decides group overflow, button width, image scaling. Portsmouth spent five rounds reverse-engineering exporter behavior by pixel-measuring preview PNGs when one export read would have caught the group overflow, button width and fluid-image behavior together in the first batch. Step numbering shifts: old step 6 'Batch report and gate' is now step 7; the 'finishing a batch IS a stop' reference at the top of the skill updated. Bumps converter 1.21.0 to 1.22.0.

drift.summary: Portsmouth v2 defect fix: render-node-not-fill constraint fires at asset export AND at module screenshot, plus logos-never-resized rule (task #31). Converter Phase 2 step 6 already carried the render-node-not-fill rule; Phase 3 step 1 (screenshot the module) now carries it too, because the mistake happens where the pipeline is. Portsmouth's hero photograph was cropped out of a canvas render and the overlapping white card baked into the image, producing a ghost headline inside the picture that only surfaced at the visual check. Phase 3 step 1 now states: the module screenshot is for the worker to classify structure, not the source of image assets; any image asset a module carries is exported from its own node in isolation, not cropped from the module screenshot or a canvas render. A bulk canvas-crop pass for efficiency in either phase is the failure mode. Separately: Phase 2 step 6 adds 'logos have an intrinsic size and are never resized to fit', because a Portsmouth 'grow inset images to fill their column' pass stretched the footer logo to 191x68. Logo intrinsic size is the source of truth; do not stretch, scale up to match a hero, or fold into a bulk image-sizing pass. Bumps converter 1.20.0 to 1.21.0.

drift.summary: Portsmouth v2 defect fix: type ramp censused instead of sampled (task #30). Audit Step 6 type-ramp bullet rewritten from sampling ('each of their text styles mapped') to a full census: enumerate every distinct (family, size, weight, line-height) tuple in the file, cluster within a point or two, treat each cluster as one ramp row. On a file with text styles the census is the styles page plus local overrides; on a file without text styles it is a walk over every text node in every design surveyed in Step 2. Report Brand foundations section note updated to say the ramp rows come from the census, not from sampled content modules. Rationale: Portsmouth ran the old skill and missed the nav-link style (15px bold) and quote style (24/38) because they never appeared in body-copy modules; the ratio test still passed because the missing sizes fell inside the existing range, so the arithmetic gate caught a distorted ramp but not an incomplete one. Census still runs on REFERENCE ONLY sources (the typefaces and weights the source uses are the palette the standard ramp gets mapped onto; sizes are discarded on that tier). Bumps audit 1.14.0 to 1.15.0.

drift.summary: Portsmouth v2 headline defect fix: spacing system census + consistency enforcement (task #27). Audit Step 6 replaces the sampled 'spacing scale from padding/spacer components' bullet with a full census read from every module in Step 5, clustered by role (section side padding, vertical rhythm, gutter, card or inset padding, mobile equivalents). Step 7 report gets a new required 'Spacing system' section between Scale factor and Module inventory, same shape as Scale factor (census, proposed system, outliers, designer decision). Any mobile value > 160px flagged. Converter Phase 2 now states every module builds on the audit's Spacing system, not per-module source values; Phase 3 step 5 verification walks the built module and asserts every side padding, vertical padding and gutter resolves to a system value (or a named exception), and flags mobile paddings > 160px. Named exceptions (full-bleed image bands, wide-quote outsets) allowed only where the audit listed them. Bumps audit 1.13.0 to 1.14.0 and converter 1.19.3 to 1.20.0. Portsmouth ran the old skills and passed every batch report while shipping 30 distinct side insets across 28 modules, one broken on mobile (220/221 on a 320 viewport): the per-module measurement was exactly how it happened.

renderSpecIsCanonical: The render rules (structure.md and references/render-spec.md here) are the single source of truth. The Codex plugin carries mirrored copies. When a render rule changes, change it here first, then regenerate the Codex references rather than hand-editing them, so the two cannot disagree.
